Explore the memos repository at /bench/repo. Give me:
1. Top-level directory listing
2. List all files under proto/api/v1/ (just filenames)
3. List all directories under server/
4. List all directories under store/

Be thorough - I need a complete map of the codebase structure. Report all findings.

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
Here is the complete codebase map for the memos repository at `/bench/repo`.

---

## 1. Top-Level Directory Listing

```
/bench/repo/
  .dockerignore
  .git/
  .github/
  .gitignore
  .golangci.yaml
  .release-please-manifest.json
  AGENTS.md
  CHANGELOG.md
  CODEOWNERS
  LICENSE
  README.md
  SECURITY.md
  cmd/             -- CLI entry point (Go)
  docs/            -- documentation
  go.mod           -- Go module definition
  go.sum
  internal/        -- internal Go packages
  proto/           -- protobuf definitions
  release-please-config.json
  scripts/         -- build/release scripts
  server/          -- HTTP server (Go)
  store/           -- data access layer (Go)
  web/             -- frontend (TypeScript/React)
```

This is a Go backend + React/TypeScript frontend monorepo for "Memos", an open-source, lightweight note-taking service.

---

## 2. Files Under `proto/api/v1/`

```
README.md
ai_service.proto
attachment_service.proto
auth_service.proto
common.proto
idp_service.proto
instance_service.proto
memo_service.proto
shortcut_service.proto
user_service.proto
```

Nine proto files defining the gRPC/Connect API surface for: AI, attachments, authentication, identity providers, instance management, memos (the core entity), shortcuts, and users.

---

## 3. All Directories Under `server/`

```
server/
server/auth                        -- authentication logic
server/notification                -- notification system
server/router/                     -- HTTP routing
server/router/api/                 -- API router
server/router/api/v1/              -- v1 API handlers (main API surface)
server/router/api/v1/test/         -- API tests
server/router/fileserver/          -- static file serving
server/router/frontend/            -- frontend SPA serving
server/router/frontend/dist/       -- embedded frontend build
server/router/mcp/                 -- MCP (Model Context Protocol) support
server/router/mcp/evals/           -- MCP evaluation tests
server/router/rss/                 -- RSS feed generation
server/runner/                     -- background task runners
server/runner/memopayload/         -- memo payload processing runner
server/runner/s3presign/           -- S3 presigned URL runner
```

Top-level server files:
- `/bench/repo/server/server.go` -- server setup and lifecycle
- `/bench/repo/server/cors.go` -- CORS configuration
- `/bench/repo/server/cors_test.go`

The `server/router/api/v1/` directory contains 60+ files implementing all API service handlers, including: `memo_service.go`, `user_service.go`, `auth_service.go`, `attachment_service.go`, `ai_service.go`, `idp_service.go`, `instance_service.go`, `shortcut_service.go`, SSE (server-sent events) hub/handler, Connect handler/interceptors, and many supporting helpers.

---

## 4. All Directories Under `store/`

```
store/
store/cache/                       -- caching layer
store/db/                          -- database drivers
store/db/mysql/                    -- MySQL driver (17 files)
store/db/postgres/                 -- PostgreSQL driver (17 files)
store/db/sqlite/                   -- SQLite driver (17 files)
store/migration/                   -- schema migrations
store/migration/mysql/             -- MySQL migrations (versions 0.17-0.28, 0.30)
store/migration/postgres/          -- PostgreSQL migrations (versions 0.19-0.28, 0.30)
store/migration/sqlite/            -- SQLite migrations (versions 0.2-0.28, 0.30)
store/seed/                        -- seed data
store/seed/sqlite/                 -- SQLite seed data
store/test/                        -- store tests
```

Top-level store files (the domain models / repository interfaces):
- `attachment.go`, `auth_config.go`, `cache.go`, `common.go`, `deployment_config.go`, `driver.go`, `idp.go`, `inbox.go`, `instance_setting.go`, `memo.go`, `memo_relation.go`, `memo_share.go`, `migrator.go`, `reaction.go`, `store.go`, `user.go`, `user_delete.go`, `user_identity.go`, `user_setting.go`

Each DB driver directory (mysql, postgres, sqlite) mirrors these domain files with driver-specific SQL implementations.

---

## 5. Files Under `web/src/`

**Top-level files:**
- `App.tsx` -- root React component
- `auth-state.ts` -- authentication state management
- `connect.ts` -- Connect (gRPC-web) client setup
- `i18n.ts` -- internationalization setup
- `index.css` -- global styles
- `main.tsx` -- React app entry point

**Key subdirectories:**

| Directory | Contents |
|-----------|----------|
| `components/` | 37 top-level component files + 22 component subdirectories (ActivityCalendar, AttachmentLibrary, ColumnGrid, ConfirmDialog, Inbox, MemoActionMenu, MemoContent, MemoDetailSidebar, MemoEditor, MemoExplorer, MemoMetadata, MemoPreview, MemoReactionListView, MemoView, PagedMemoList, Placeholder, Settings, StatisticsView, UserMemoMap, kit, map, ui) |
| `hooks/` | 26 hook files: useMemoQueries, useUserQueries, useAttachmentLibrary, useAttachmentQueries, useLiveMemoRefresh, useMemoFilters, useMemoSorting, useMemoShareQueries, useInstanceQueries, useIdentityProviderQueries, useDialog, useCurrentUser, useNavigateTo, useTokenRefreshOnFocus, useUserLocale, useUserTheme, and more |
| `pages/` | 16 page components: Home, Explore, MemoDetail, SignIn, SignUp, AdminSignIn, AuthCallback, Setting, Archived, Attachments, Inboxes, Shortcuts, UserProfile, About, NotFound, PermissionDenied |

## 7. Main Entry Point / Server Startup

**`/bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go`** (219 lines)

This is the application entry point. Key structure:

- Uses **Cobra** for CLI commands and **Viper** for configuration (flags, env vars, defaults).
- The `rootCmd` is the main command that:
  1. Builds a `profile.Profile` from configuration (demo mode, addr, port, unix socket, data dir, database driver, DSN, instance URL).
  2. Creates a database driver via `db.NewDBDriver(instanceProfile)` -- supports sqlite (default), mysql, and postgres.
  3. Initializes the store with `store.New(dbDriver, instanceProfile)`.
  4. Runs database migrations with `storeInstance.Migrate(ctx)`.
  5. Loads deployment configuration with `storeInstance.LoadDeploymentConfiguration(ctx)`.
  6. Creates and starts the HTTP server with `server.NewServer(ctx, instanceProfile, storeInstance)`.
  7. Listens for SIGINT/SIGTERM for graceful shutdown.
- Default port is **8081**, default driver is **sqlite**.
- Environment variables are prefixed with `MEMOS_` (e.g., `MEMOS_PORT`, `MEMOS_DRIVER`).
- A `version` subcommand prints the current version.
- Logging uses `slog` with configurable log level.

## Architecture Summary

- **Backend**: Go monolith with Cobra CLI, Connect/gRPC API (proto-defined), three database backends (SQLite/MySQL/PostgreSQL), and a versioned migration system.
- **Frontend**: React + TypeScript SPA using Connect (gRPC-web) for API communication, React Query for data fetching, and React Context for state management. No Redux or Zustand -- hooks and contexts are the state management approach.
- **API**: Defined in protobuf under `proto/api/v1/`, with generated TypeScript types in `web/src/types/proto/` and Go server handlers in `server/router/api/v1/`.
- **Notable features**: SSE for live updates, MCP support, RSS feeds, AI integration, identity provider (SSO) support, S3 storage, motion photo handling.
